correctness.rationale: The local-matchings proof exhausts all \(2^{16}\) bijections at the sixteen four-bit vertices and retains exactly those yielding a single 32-edge Euler circuit; each de Bruijn cycle is uniquely canonically rooted at 00000. A second edge-disjoint Euler-tour DFS independently enumerates all 2048 cycles. Two independent longest-circular-palindrome computations agree word by word; the complete integer histogram and all size-two/size-four reversal/complement orbits are asserted in the replayed standard-library code. The forced circular factor 1000001 analytically proves the common lower bound seven. All statements are finite at order five.

originality.rationale: A material reading of Anisiu–Anisiu–Kása (2010 arXiv HTML) yields generation of palindromes from de Bruijn words and general finite-word palindrome complexity, but no order-five longest-circular-palindrome profile. Simpson (2014) and OEIS A247000 study the count of distinct palindromes in unrestricted circular words, not maximum factor length over de Bruijn cycles. Targeted mathematical-record queries find different problems (rich-word maxima, palindrome-duplication codes, Sturmian palindrome collapse), not this histogram. The published and prior exact order-five BWT run spectrum concerns runs of a transformation, not palindrome length of the original cycle. Potential prior unindexed tables and inaccessible Simpson full text are residual originality risks; not treated as proofs of novelty.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed or differently named complete order-five palindrome-length table may exist; search cannot establish uniqueness.
The complete text of Simpson (2014) was not available for inspection; its abstract describes a distinct invariant but an appendix could contain related finite data.

value.rationale: The longest circular palindromic factor is a natural reversal-symmetry invariant of universal cycles. The complete 2048-cycle census gives an exact distribution rather than one maximizer, sharp endpoints 7 and 15, an unattainable intermediate value 14, and the full 528-orbit classification under reversal and complement. The forced length-seven palindrome explains the unavoidable baseline; the exact finite spectrum is independently useful as a benchmark for reversal-aware universal-cycle constructions and palindromic-avoidance problems. Its distribution cannot be deduced from the classical count of de Bruijn cycles, distinct-palindrome bounds, or the BWT run distribution.
